definitions.gloss: in a fluster; hurriedly; in a panic
definitions.explanation: An onomatopoeic adverb describing a state of flustered, panicky movement, rushing about without composure.

examples.japanese: あたふたと{準備|じゅんび}する。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{時間|じかん}に{遅|おく}れそうで、あたふた{走|はし}った。
examples.english: I was about to miss the train, so I ran about frantically.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}な{来客|らいきゃく}に、{母|はは}はあたふたと{部屋|へや}を{片付|かたづ}け{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Caught off guard by unexpected guests, my mother frantically started tidying up the room.

notes:
An onomatopoeic adverb (オノマトペ) conveying the image of someone rushing around in a flustered, disorganized manner. Often used with the particle と.

USAGE:
- あたふたする (to be in a fluster — used as a suru verb)
- あたふたと (in a fluster — used as an adverb modifying a verb)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- あたふたと{逃|に}げる (flee in a panic)
- あたふたと{支度|したく}する (get ready in a rush)
- あたふたと{走|はし}り{回|まわ}る (run around frantically)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- おろおろ — being at a loss, confused and helpless (less action-oriented, more standing in bewilderment)
- ばたばた — rushing about busily (can be neutral busy-ness, not necessarily panicked)
- そわそわ — restlessly, fidgeting (anxiety-based rather than action-based)
- {大慌|おおあわ}て — great panic (noun describing the same state)
